extracted.intended_audience: judges, patent litigators, and academics who draft or evaluate jury instructions and damages analyses in patent cases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for drafting and applying jury instructions and evidentiary practices to determine reasonable royalty patent damages (focus on avoiding ex post bias, ensuring apportionment, and making instructions comprehensible and reviewable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit or avoid verbatim Georgia-Pacific recitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The fifteen Georgia-Pacific factors are unprioritized, often overlapping, may not all apply in every case, and verbatim recitation overloads juries with factors that may be irrelevant, overlapping, or contradictory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on rote recitation of the Georgia-Pacific factors; recognize many factors may be inapposite or require molding to fit case facts. Provide a simpler, cohesive framework instead of listing many factors without guidance on weighting or application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude ex post considerations (generally)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions should exclude ex post considerations such as lock-in costs and litigation risk that arise after the hypothetical negotiation date because they tend to inflate royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit consideration of ex post information (e.g., actual commercial success) only to the extent it "sheds light on what the parties would have expected and agreed upon ex ante," and only if its use would not on balance be prejudicial or confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus the jury on the ex ante market value of the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate issue for jurors is determining the market value of the patent before the alleged infringement — i.e., the value at the hypothetical ex ante negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hypothetical negotiation as a device to focus jurors on what parties would have agreed to ex ante; avoid using factors that incorporate post-infringement realities except as limited above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment / incremental value requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The market value of a patent is based on, and cannot be greater than, the incremental value of the patented technology over available alternatives; royalties must be specifically based on the value of the patented features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require evidence separating or apportioning the patentee's damages between patented and unpatented features (e.g., smallest salable patent-practicing unit and further apportionment if that unit contains unrelated noninfringing features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude value contributed by non-patented elements and other non-inventive factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions should clearly exclude value contributed by factors other than the claimed invention (technical components not claimed, manufacturing process, product marketing, brand recognition, conventional elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell jurors to ignore benefits of conventional elements or benefits obtainable via noninfringing alternatives when determining the patent's market value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat alternatives as a fundamental ceiling on royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives to the patented technology provide a fundamental constraint on what a willing licensee would pay ex ante — i.e., a ceiling on the royalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruct jurors to consider the best alternative available at the hypothetical negotiation date and not to treat availability of alternatives as merely one factor among many; jurors should not award more than the value of the patented technology relative to that alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate hypothetical negotiation date (avoid lock-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypothetical negotiation date should be set to avoid including lock-in costs; it should be the time before the alleged infringer was committed to using the claimed technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid setting the date at first sale or at a time when the implementer was already locked-in. For SEPs, set the date just before the patent became essential to the relevant standard rather than the date of first infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use of actual ex post profits; focus on expected excess profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on actual post-hoc profits as the measure of the patent's contribution; instead, assess the excess profit expected at the time of the hypothetical negotiation beyond the next-best alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit inquiry to expectations about profits rather than actual ex post experience that would not have influenced the ex ante bargain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gatekeep comparable-license evidence for ex post infection and comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparable licenses and an established licensing royalty may inform the jury, but the court should ensure licenses are truly comparable and not 'infected' by ex post considerations that inflate price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruct jurors to consider whether licenses were negotiated after the licensor had locked-in the licensee or were affected by litigation risk; the trial court should exclude license agreements so infected when their prejudice outweighs their probative value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity, cohesion, and plain language in instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Jury instructions should be simple, use less legal vernacular, be tailored to the facts, and clearly identify the relevant considerations in a cohesive framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use psycholinguistic principles to rewrite and simplify instructions; avoid complex multi-factor lists without explanation of how to weigh them so jurors can comprehend and apply the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require documentation of jury findings to improve reviewability
rubrics_metrics.description: When juries are not instructed to document findings on each factor or how they weighed factors, determinations become a 'black box' that is difficult to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider instructing jurors to record findings or provide a framework that makes the basis for the award reviewable to facilitate meaningful appellate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn against reliance on licenses negotiated after implementer committed to technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses negotiated after an implementer was committed to the technology may reflect inflated prices due to lock-in and litigation risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell jurors to discount or be skeptical of such post-commitment licenses and explain how such licenses may overstate what parties would have agreed ex ante.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize cognitive biases (hindsight, outcome, anchoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of ex post information increases the risk of hindsight bias, outcome bias, and anchoring on patent-holder demands, which can distort jury assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret factors in light of the best alternative available at the time of the hypothetical ex ante negotiation and design instructions to minimize these biases (e.g., limit ex post evidence and use clear framing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical guidance on calculating reasonable royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions should give jurors helpful, practical directions on how to calculate a reasonable royalty rather than only abstract factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the parts of model instructions (e.g., N.D. Cal.) that offer concrete calculation guidance while correcting their shortcomings (e.g., on date selection and apportionment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) and RAND constraints specially
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Georgia-Pacific factors are inappropriate or contrary to RAND principles in SEP cases; special adjustments (date and apportionment) are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SEPs, set the hypothetical negotiation date to just before the patent became essential to the standard, emphasize apportionment, and account for RAND obligations when instructing jurors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the 'contingent ex ante' (hybrid) approach
rubrics_metrics.description: A hybrid approach that asks jurors to reconstruct an ex ante bargain with ex post information is inferior because it asks jurors to imagine a bargain that could not have existed and tends to overweight ex post events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a pure ex ante approach; if ex post information is used it should be only to illustrate what parties would have expected ex ante, subject to safeguards against undue weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat alternatives, comparables, or profits as unstructured factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain considerations (alternatives, comparable licenses, expected profits) should not be buried as one factor among many without specifying their constraining or apportionment roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly instruct jurors how each such consideration constrains the royalty (e.g., alternatives cap the royalty; apportionment limits award to incremental value) rather than leaving them to weigh unstructured factors.
